memory_update.text: Core direct candidates for the advanced_foundry_packaging_lithography node: TSM, ASML, AMAT, KLAC, AMKR.
The node appears to split into three investable sub-layers: foundry/packaging asset owners, lithography/WFE tool vendors, and process-control/OSAT capacity enablers.

Next pass should check additional US-listed or ADR candidates not included due to the five-name cap: LRCX, ONTO, ASMIY/ASM International, TOELY/Tokyo Electron, ASX/ASE Technology, UMC, ICHR, COHU, TER, AEHR, FORM, MKSI, ENTG, ACLS, and substrate/interposer suppliers where US listing and market cap are sufficient.

Need separate evidence pass for advanced substrates/interposers because many obvious leaders are Japan/Taiwan-listed rather than primarily US-listed; ADR liquidity and market-cap eligibility should be checked.
Amkor's inclusion is an inference rather than a fully proven AI bottleneck claim because Arizona capacity is not immediate and customer/product mix must be verified through future disclosures.

Core US-listed/ADR names for advanced foundry, packaging and lithography chokepoint: TSM, ASML, AMAT, LRCX, ONTO. KLA and AMKR should remain next-pass candidates if the dashboard allows more than five.

The node has at least four separable bottleneck layers: leading-edge wafer capacity, EUV lithography tool availability, advanced-packaging process equipment/metrology, and OSAT/package assembly capacity.

Need a separate pass on substrate/interposer suppliers and non-US-listed but US-accessible ADRs/OTC names such as ASE Technology, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron and substrate materials vendors; many key bottleneck suppliers may not be standard US exchange listings.

Need to verify whether KLA should replace or join ONTO in the final universe; KLA has strong process-control relevance and official FY2025 materials mention AI infrastructure and advanced packaging growth.
Add AMKR as a high-priority direct AI advanced-packaging capacity candidate; evidence includes 2025 10-K AI/HPC advanced-packaging language and Arizona advanced-packaging campus.
Add ONTO as a second-order but evidence-backed metrology/inspection candidate tied to HBM and advanced packaging; $240M HBM VPA is a key evidence anchor.

Add ENTG and MKSI as underappreciated second-order suppliers to advanced nodes, EUV/lithography, process purity, electronics/packaging and substrate-related tool chains; keep claim type below fact for AI-specific exposure until revenue attribution is verified.
Advanced packaging chokepoint should be tracked across OSAT capacity, HBM bump/metrology, substrate/PCB processing, EUV reticle/wafer purity, and yield-control software/tools, not just TSMC and ASML.

Need a separate non-US or ADR pass for substrate/interposer suppliers such as Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Nan Ya PCB, AT&S and Ajinomoto-like materials exposure; many are not straightforward US-listed common equities.
